analysis.title: Marketcolour + M&A Basket/Global Macro: Gjensidige / Wartsila / Allianz / Orange / Apple
key_insights: US equities closed higher Monday: SPX +70bps to 7676, NDX +109bps to 29273, RTY +38bps to 2786. 7 of 11 sectors rose, with Industrials +1.40% and Consumer Discretionary +1.11% leading and Communication Services -1.42% lagging.
Brazilian EWZ fell 20%, its worst session outside of covid, after President Lula won the Brazil election. BRLUSD fell another 9%.
Breadth recovered, a sign of stabilization in the AI trade. The GS Data Center Basket (GSTMTDAT) rose 2.60% and the AI Semis basket (GSCBSMHX) rose 2.52%.
In Europe, EU Defense (GSSBDEFE) rose 2.4% and EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) rose 2.3%. French Banks (GSXEFRBK) rose 2% and stabilised on Moody's relief.

Since 2024, alternative trading systems (dark pools) gained 2.3% of US equities market share by shares and 3.5% by notional. OTC share gains were negligible at +0.1% by shares, and OTC lost 2.8% of notional share over the same period.
Flow: there are still few signs of offense being played across AI and Tech. The bounces of the last 2 weeks are mostly driven by the end of high-velocity supply.

M&A basket (GSTRACQN) additions: Abivax, Haleon, Moncler, Burberry, Prada, Swatch Group, Rightmove, Scout24 and Zegona. About 65% of the basket is Industrials, Consumer Discretionary and Healthcare, and about 35% is UK-domiciled.

Asset allocation stays modestly pro-risk: overweight equities for 3m/12m, underweight credit for 3m/12m, overweight cash for 3m and overweight bonds for 12m. AI concerns, Middle East tensions and mid-term elections could sustain near-term volatility, but earnings support, lighter positioning and lower valuations should help equities into year-end.

Global growth has been 'remarkably unremarkable' in 2026, with fiscal easing and the AI boom offsetting drags from energy and tariffs. The 2027 baseline is a similar pace, with downside risks from higher energy prices, higher bond yields and slower AI investment growth.
With AI labor market effects more visible and inflation likely to decline, GS expects fewer rate hikes than priced for most major developed-market central banks.

Gjensidige: GS expects the pricing environment to normalise as claims inflation moderates. Earn-through of prior pricing should keep supporting profitability, but margin expansion should become more measured. GS cuts FY27e-30e EPS by about 2.4% on average.

Wartsila Q3: orders +45% vs consensus +33% and organic growth +16% vs consensus +13%. Reported sales were in line and margin of 14.2% was 10bps above consensus 14.1%, a 1% beat. The orders beat came entirely from Energy, while Marine was weaker on Equipment orders. Guidance is unchanged.
Allianz 3Q'26 results are due November 12. GS operating profit estimate is about 1% below company-collected consensus, driven by P&C (-2%) and Asset Management (-2%).

Orange beat and raised its EBITDA guide, pointing to a possible fourth consecutive quarter of beat and raise. Revenue was €12.19B, helped by Spain 1.9% ahead and France 1.1% ahead. EBITDAaL was €4.14B (+4.6%), 0.9% ahead, and OFCF was 1% ahead.
Apple preview: GS expects in-line F4Q26 results with iPhone revenue +15% y/y, Services revenue +10% y/y and gross margin of 47.8%.

market_movers.rationale: Gjensidige moved to Neutral (DG to N) with a 5% upside to target. GS expects claims inflation to moderate and margin expansion to slow, and cut FY27e-30e EPS by about 2.4%.
Allianz pre-earnings note with 10% upside. GS 3Q'26 operating profit estimate is about 1% below consensus on P&C and Asset Management.
GS expects in-line F4Q26 results with iPhone +15% y/y, Services +10% y/y and gross margin of 47.8%. Upside to target is 15%.

earnings_insights: Wartsila Q3 (reported): orders +45% vs consensus +33%, organic growth +16% vs consensus +13%, reported sales in line, margin 14.2% vs consensus 14.1%, about a 1% beat. Orders strength was entirely Energy, Marine was weaker on Equipment orders. Guidance unchanged.

Allianz 3Q'26 (preview, results due 11/12): GS operating profit estimate is about 1% below company-collected consensus published 10/26/26. P&C is -2% with a COR about 15bps less favourable and insurance revenue about 2% lower. Asset Management is -2%.
Orange (reported): revenue €12.19B, with Spain 1.9% ahead and France 1.1% ahead of consensus. EBITDAaL €4.14B (+4.6%), 0.9% ahead. OFCF 1% ahead. EBITDA guidance raised.
Apple F4Q26 (preview, GS estimates): iPhone revenue +15% y/y, Services revenue +10% y/y, gross margin 47.8%. GS expects results in line.
Gjensidige: GS cut FY27e-30e EPS by about 2.4% on average on lower growth and margin expansion.
